card: Removes time-based mempool transaction expiry along with the -mempoolexpiry configuration option and the mempool's entry_time index. Age-based eviction is incentive-incompatible because it discards transactions that are still mineable, such as low-feerate parents waiting for CPFP fee bumps. Dropping the index reduces memory overhead per transaction entry, allowing more transactions to fit into the configured -maxmempool budget. The -mempoolexpiry option is kept as a hidden no-op that logs a startup warning.
changed_since_previous: No substantial architectural changes; commit organization and functional test adaptations were refreshed.
evidence: Author description and commit 1c110f155b: 'Evicting mempool transactions by age (-mempoolexpiry, default two weeks) is incentive-incompatible: it may drop transactions that could still be mined', citing issue #33510 ('Mempool Expiry eviction might remove txs that could be mined in the next block').

Author notes secondary benefit in description: 'The DynamicMemoryUsage() per-entry estimate drops from three indexes to two, so within the same -maxmempool budget the mempool fits slightly more transactions.'
problem: Age-based transaction eviction (previously defaulting to two weeks) is incentive-incompatible because it can drop mineable transactions, such as low-feerate parents waiting for child-pays-for-parent fee bumps. Maintaining the unused `entry_time` index also consumes memory for an ordered-tree node and causes O(log n) overhead on every mempool insertion and deletion.

risk.why: Alters mempool transaction eviction policy and memory accounting, which could affect mempool contents and size limit enforcement.

scope_notes: Deletes the functional test mempool_expiry.py and rewires USDT and wallet resend functional tests to test eviction and resubmission via replacement rather than expiry.
summary: Removes time-based mempool transaction expiry and the `-mempoolexpiry` option. Deletes the `entry_time` multi-index container and its comparator from `CTxMemPool`, updating `DynamicMemoryUsage` accounting from three indexes to two. Retains `-mempoolexpiry` as a hidden no-op setting that logs an initialization warning if provided.
